## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga belonging to the desmids, characterized by exceptionally long, slender cells divided into two symmetrical semicells by a narrow central constriction. Each semicell tapers toward the end and typically terminates in three short spines, giving Triploceras gracile a distinctive elongated appearance. It occurs in freshwater habitats such as ponds, shallow wetlands, and other standing waters and has been recorded widely in tropical and subtropical regions. Like other desmids, it contributes to primary production and forms part of the microscopic food web in freshwater ecosystems.
